title: Inverse image induced by a continuous left-exact site functor and its tensor structure
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] whose objects and morphisms are small in one universe; take sheaves of sets and abelian groups in a larger universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Suppose $\mathcal C$ has finite limits and $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserves them and sends coverings to coverings. Then left Kan extension along $u^{op}$ followed by sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] exists and gives a functor $L:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ left adjoint to $G\mapsto G\circ u^{op}$. The functor $L$ preserves finite limits and all colimits, so this adjunction is a geometric morphism $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$. On abelian sheaves the same construction is additive and exact. With sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], there are canonical isomorphisms $L(F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}G)\cong LF\otimes_{\mathbf Z}LG$ and $L\underline{\mathbf Z}\cong\underline{\mathbf Z}$, giving a strong symmetric monoidal structure. Under these tensor structures, the inverse-image composition and identity isomorphisms compatible with the adjunctions are monoidal natural isomorphisms, for composable functors satisfying the same hypotheses.

proof.text: Apply flat_of_preservesFiniteLimits. Its comma categories are filtered. The proved general-universe instance preservesFiniteLimits_op_lan_of_flat applies to sets and abelian groups: shrink AB5 from size (u+1,u+1) to (u,u+1), the comma-category size. The composite with the sheaf inclusion and sheafification preserves finite limits. The set and abelian adjunctions give colimits. Abelian pushforward is additive on sectionwise morphisms, so left_adjoint_additive gives additive pullback. Preservation of finite limits and finite colimits then gives ShortExact.map_of_exact. This is the finite-limit Kan-extension argument of 00X6, without the auxiliary abelian-group-object lifting route.

proof.text: Forgetting module structure on either site is left adjoint to sectionwise coinduction, by the proved Sheaf.forget₂CoinduceAdj. Compose module pullback with the forgetful adjunction on D, and compose the forgetful adjunction on C with abelian pullback. Their right adjoints are definitionally equal, because sectionwise coinduction commutes with precomposition. The uniqueness isomorphism a.leftAdjointUniq b gives exactly the required natural isomorphism between module pullback followed by forgetting and forgetting followed by abelian pullback. No arbitrary object is chosen from an existence theorem.

proof.text: Use the localized monoidal structure Sheaf.monoidalCategory and its braiding. Filtered comma categories are sifted; tensoring in ModuleCat is a left adjoint because modules form a closed monoidal category, so it preserves the required colimits. The existing proved sheafPullbackMonoidal supplies the strong monoidal structure; its underlying oplax structure is definitionally sheafPullbackOplaxMonoidal. Its proof identifies the oplax comparison with the Kan-extension tensor comparison followed by monoidal sheafification, so this is the stated sheaf tensor. The canonical pullback-pushforward adjunction is monoidal and pushforward is lax braided. Adjunction.μ_comp_map_braiding gives the braided axiom for pullback. Choose these canonical structures, with all normalization equalities reflexive.

proof.text: For composable U,V, establish continuity and representable flatness and use the same canonical strong monoidal structures for U,V,U⋙V and the identity. The proved pushforward comparison sheafPushforwardContinuousComp' (Iso.refl _) is monoidal. Conjugate it between the composite pullback adjunction and the pullback adjunction of U⋙V. The resulting isomorphism has the direction required in the statement; isMonoidal_conjugateEquiv_symm makes it monoidal. unit_conjugateEquiv_symm identifies its unit; the pushforward comparison has identity components, so its formula reduces to the iterated units. For the identity, conjugate the inverse of sheafPushforwardContinuousId' (Iso.refl _) between Adjunction.id and the identity-site pullback adjunction. That pushforward comparison is monoidal, hence so is its conjugate, and the same unit equation reduces to the inverse of sheafPushforwardContinuousId. These are calculations with adjunction units, not an assertion that pullback is sectionwise precomposition.
